description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Opengrep SARIF fixture that carries one record with no usable message. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. Key names follow expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json, the template every negative file in this folder reuses, so one generic loader reads them all; the three blocks specific to this condition -- message_variants, no_synthesised_message and never_absent_content_field_trio -- are additive.

fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from the captured one rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. /runs/0/results/1 is unmodified captured output: compared as canonical JSON it is identical to harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif results[432] and to the positive fixture's results[1]. /runs/0/results/0 is the synthesized defective record: the OneForOneBlockPusher.java carrier that the sibling negative fixtures share, with its message.text replaced by the empty string. It is the only defective record here, and its message is the only thing defective about it.
fixture.carrier_record: Six fixtures in this folder place a record at this same location -- reject-sarif-malformed-record.sarif results[3], reject-sarif-missing-rule-id.sarif results[2], reject-sarif-uribaseid-cycle.sarif results[1], reject-sarif-uribaseid-missing-base.sarif results[1], reject-sarif-uribaseid-relative-no-absolute-ancestor.sarif results[1], and this fixture's results[0] -- so the carrier is named rather than left to be noticed. Reusing one record shape is what makes a single field the difference between two fixtures. It does not make the carrier defective everywhere: in three of the six it becomes an ordinary row, and in reject-sarif-missing-rule-id.sarif it is a surviving row that resolves its rule through ruleIndex rather than ruleId.
fixture.nearest_neighbour: reject-sarif-malformed-record.sarif's carrier is this record with its message replaced by a string rather than emptied, and it is rejected there under malformed_record with the detail "the result's message is a string, not an object". The two fixtures therefore draw the missing_message / malformed_record boundary with the same record and one field's difference: an object with no usable text is an absent message, and a message that is not an object at all is a wrong shape.
fixture.carrier_carries_its_own_level: This fixture's carrier additionally carries a level of "error" of its own, and it is the only one of the six that does. That is deliberate rather than incidental: it closes the last route by which the record could have been degraded for a reason other than its message, since its severity is resolvable from the record itself without consulting its rule.
fixture.captured_provenance: The defective record appears in neither harness/artifacts/raw/opengrep.sarif nor oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/opengrep.sarif. Checked structurally against all 1322 results of the artifact with the message key ignored, so a captured record differing from it only in its message would still have been found and none was -- which is what makes this record demonstrably the fixture's own addition rather than something the tool emitted. The real artifact carries no result with an absent or empty message at all, and exactly one hardcoded-conditional result, at common/network-common/src/main/java/org/apache/spark/network/buffer/FileSegmentManagedBuffer.java:112. The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these values are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.
fixture.not_records: The three entries under /runs/0/invocations/0/toolExecutionNotifications are tool notifications -- two syntax errors and one rule timeout over vendored minified JavaScript -- and are not finding records. They are neither rows nor rejections and are not counted. Each of them does carry a message.text, which is exactly why they are named here rather than passed over: a traversal that counted anything message-shaped would arrive at five records, and this fixture would then appear to reject one message out of five rather than one out of two.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape.is_sarif -- a version of "2.1.0" together with a runs array; those two together are the whole test
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route("opengrep", doc) returns tool "opengrep", shape "sarif", adapter "sarif", scanner_class "sast"
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No normalize.shape.UnknownArtifactShape is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is valid SARIF 2.1.0 and routes cleanly; exactly one record inside it is defective, and the adapter rejects that record while still emitting the other. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py and does not use this fixture.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS, and message being one of them is the whole reason this fixture's defective record cannot become a row.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob the emitted row matched is recorded under row_derivations, and the glob the rejected record's path would have matched is recorded under rejections -- recorded there precisely because it never becomes an in_scope value.

resolution_context.root_independence: The surviving uri is already root-relative, and the recorded path base for opengrep is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the uri unchanged. This row therefore holds for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file. The rejected record is root-independent for a different reason: it is classified at the message step, before any base is consulted, so no choice of root changes its outcome.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the opengrep entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.uri_base_id_walk_consequence: With no run.originalUriBaseIds the SARIF 2.1.0 section 3.4.4 procedure cannot complete -- the documented producer gap -- and that outcome is eligible for the metadata-backed fallback, so the resolvable path resolves against the runner-recorded base rather than being rejected. The defective record never reaches this walk: the message step precedes the path step in the adapter's fixed order.
resolution_context.severity_source: The surviving result states no level of its own and its rule carries no properties.severity or properties.problem.severity, so severity_native is the level its rule states under defaultConfiguration.level and severity_norm comes from the SARIF level table: error High, warning Medium, note Low, none Info.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A SARIF result names a code location rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry.

rejection_boundary.statement: A record with no usable message is a rejection. It is not a row carrying an empty message, and it is not a row carrying a message assembled from somewhere else. This fixture exists to fix that outcome, because both alternatives are reachable in one line of code and neither is detectable downstream once written.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: AAP 0.8.2 fixes the closed set of fields permitted to be absent, and emit.py encodes it: OPTIONAL_FIELDS is exactly severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve and package_coordinate, and message is not among them -- it is in emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS. So no valid row representation of a record without a message exists at all. emit.py rejects a required field that is null or blank rather than writing it, which leaves exactly two other outcomes, and both hide the record: dropping it silently breaks raw == rows + rejections, and manufacturing a message asserts something the tool never said. Counting it under a named class is the only outcome that keeps the record visible and the arithmetic honest.
rejection_boundary.not_the_same_as_an_absent_optional: A row whose severity_native, start_line, cwe, cve or package_coordinate is null is an ordinary row, and this fixture's surviving row is one -- three of its five optionals are null. The distinction is the closed set, not the shape of the value: null in an optional field is the absence convention working, null in message would be a schema violation.
rejection_boundary.not_a_malformed_record: A message that is not an object at all -- a string, a number, an array -- is malformed_record rather than missing_message. _message_text draws that line itself, and the two classes are kept apart because a reader of tool-status.md acts differently on "this producer omits message text" than on "this artifact is not shaped like SARIF". This fixture's defective record carries a message object, so it is squarely the missing_message case.
rejection_boundary.no_synthesised_content: Nothing in this file supplies a message for the rejected record, not even a plausible one. The candidate strings a synthesiser would reach for are listed under no_synthesised_message so a test can assert their absence, never so that one can be adopted.
rejection_boundary.no_dropped_record: The rejected record is counted, not discarded. rejections is 1 and rejections_by_class names the class, so the record survives in the record even though it produces no row.

message_variants.authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, _message_text -- the single function every SARIF message passes through. The class is the same for every route that ends in a message the artifact does not carry; the detail is what distinguishes them, which is why a test asserts the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings.
message_variants.no_template_is_rendered: Where a producer supplies message.id and message.arguments but no text, the message is treated as absent rather than formatted from the template. Rendering one would manufacture content the artifact does not carry, and the detail says so in those words.

variants.variant: message.text present as an empty or whitespace-only string
variants.expected_detail: the result's message.text is empty or whitespace only
variants.why_this_is_the_variant_worth_carrying: It is the form a real producer most likely emits, and the one a loose check handles inconsistently: "text" in message is true, message.get("text") is not None is true, and only a non-empty-string test rejects it. A fixture carrying only the absent-key variant would pass an adapter that wrote an empty message into a row. The blank test is on strip() while a surviving message is returned verbatim and untrimmed, so a whitespace-only text is this same variant and reaches the same class.

variants.variant: the result carries no message object at all
variants.expected_detail: the result carries no message object
variants.cover_with: a derived fixture whose defective record omits the message key entirely

variants.variant: a message object carrying no text key
variants.expected_detail: the result's message carries no text
variants.detail_extension: where the object carries id or arguments the detail continues "; it supplies only a message template, which is not rendered here because rendering one would manufacture content the artifact does not carry"
variants.cover_with: a derived fixture whose defective record carries message.id and message.arguments and no text

variants.variant: message.text present but not a string
variants.expected_detail: the result's message.text is a <json type>, not a string
variants.cover_with: a derived fixture whose defective record carries a numeric or array message.text

variants.variant: message present but not an object
variants.expected_detail: the result's message is a <json type>, not an object
variants.note: Named inside this block rather than outside it because it is the nearest neighbour of the four variants above and the only one that leaves this class. It is already covered: reject-sarif-malformed-record.sarif carries this same carrier record with a string message at its results[3], and the adapter rejects it there under malformed_record.

no_synthesised_message.prohibition: No emitted row's message may be assembled from the rule descriptor, the rule identifier, or any other part of the artifact that is not the record's own message.text. A synthesised message asserts something the tool never said, which AAP 0.1.3's reject-rather-than-infer rule forbids outright: where a record cannot be attributed with certainty it is rejected and counted, never guessed into a field.
no_synthesised_message.why_it_needs_asserting: A message is trivially manufacturable here. The defective record's rule carries a fullDescription and a shortDescription, and either would read as a plausible finding message -- so an adapter that filled the gap from the rule would produce a row that looks entirely ordinary and is wrong in the one way nothing downstream can detect.
no_synthesised_message.checked_by: substring comparison against every emitted row's message, not by inspection. Equality alone would miss a message built by concatenating a rule string with anything else.

forbidden_strings_from_the_defective_rec.fullDescription.text: This if statement will always have the same behavior and is therefore unnecessary.
forbidden_strings_from_the_defective_rec.name: opt.blitzy-harness.rules.opengrep-rules.java.lang.correctness.hardcoded-conditional
forbidden_strings_from_the_defective_rec.help.text_and_help.markdown: This if statement will always have the same behavior and is therefore unnecessary.

no_synthesised_message.verified_absent: None of those strings equals, and none is a substring of, the one emitted row's message. Verified against the fixture rather than asserted: the emitted message is the tainted-SQL text of a different rule and shares no substring with any of them.
no_synthesised_message.scoping_the_check_correctly: The comparison is scoped to the defective record's rule, /runs/0/tool/driver/rules/0. Scoped instead to every rule in the run it would false-positive, because the surviving record's message is byte-identical to its own rule's fullDescription.text and help.text -- opengrep duplicates a finding's message into its rule descriptor, so that coincidence is captured tool output rather than synthesis. A test that widened the scope would fail on a correct adapter, which is the more expensive of the two mistakes.
no_synthesised_message.the_synthesised_value_would_be_recognisa: The sibling uriBaseId fixtures carry this same carrier record with its message intact, and that message is the very sentence rules[0].fullDescription.text holds. So the string a synthesiser would produce for this fixture is known exactly, and its appearance in any row derived from this fixture is the violation rather than a coincidence.

never_absent_content_field_trio.statement: Three of the seven never-absent fields carry content read out of the record -- rule_id, message and path -- and each has its own negative fixture in this folder. The set is complete, and the grouping is stated so a reader can see that it is.
never_absent_content_field_trio.the_other_four_required_fields: tool, scanner_class, severity_norm and in_scope are the remaining members of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS and none of them is read out of a record: tool and scanner_class are stamped from the routing decision, severity_norm is defined for every input including no vocabulary at all, and in_scope is a predicate over the resolved path. None can be absent, so none needs a negative fixture -- which is what makes the trio above the whole of the required-content surface.
never_absent_content_field_trio.the_fifth_sarif_condition: non_integer_start_line is the adapter's fifth and last rejecting step, and it concerns an optional field: a start_line that is absent is a null in a row, while a start_line present and not an integer is a rejection. It is covered by reject-sarif-non-integer-start-line.sarif and is not part of this trio.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of runs[].results[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records("opengrep", doc), whose SARIF traversal sums the length of each run's results array and builds no row, resolves no path, reads no message and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. Two is also the figure a reader arrives at by hand from the fixture, and the two agreeing is the point.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.note: Named here rather than restated with their values. The counters block below is the single measurement, and a number carried twice inside one document is a number that can drift; counters_note gives the reason each of the four is zero.

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned as partial where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: the parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its parser reason retained. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's STATUS_PASS / STATUS_FAIL / STATUS_NOT_APPLICABLE vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/sarif.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty authored keys, one path_kind_* per member of paths.PATH_KINDS and one severity_basis_* per member of severity.BASIS_VALUES, twenty-nine in total.
counters_note: Three things a reader must not "correct". First, rule_id_from_rule_id is 2 while every severity counter sums to 1: the rule step is step 2 of the classification order and severity is computed only for a record that becomes a row, so the rejected record resolves its rule identifier before it is rejected and never reaches severity. That asymmetry is the classification order made visible, not a miscount. Second, severity_from_level is 0 even though the rejected record carries a level of "error" of its own -- for the same reason: the level is never read, because step 3 ends the record. Third, the four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool are all 0 here: both results carry exactly one location, so multi_location_records is 0; the one rule that names a weakness names exactly one, so multi_valued_cwe_records is 0; no rule string carries a CVE identifier, so multi_valued_cve_records is 0; and the one emitted path names a file inside the scanned tree, so non_filesystem_paths is 0. tool_component_reference_unresolved is 0 because neither result carries a rule reference at all, and an absent reference means the driver -- SARIF's own default -- rather than an unresolved component.

corroboration.note: The surviving result is a captured result the positive sibling also covers -- this file's row 0 is that file's row 1 -- and all twelve field comparisons agree. Recorded after the fact rather than as the source of these values: each value here was derived from the fixture and the authored contracts, so a future disagreement between this file and the adapter is a finding to diagnose rather than a diff to apply. The rejected record has no counterpart to corroborate against: it is this fixture's own synthesized addition, it appears in no captured artifact, and it contributes no dataset row.

rows.message: User data flows into this manually-constructed SQL string. User data can be safely inserted into SQL strings using prepared statements or an object-relational mapper (ORM). Manually-constructed SQL strings is a possible indicator of SQL injection, which could let an attacker steal or manipulate data from the database. Instead, use prepared statements (`connection.PreparedStatement`) or a safe library.

row_derivations.rule_id_source: the result's own ruleId; no ruleIndex and no rule reference is present
row_derivations.message_is_the_tool_s_own_words: The message is the text opengrep wrote, carried verbatim and untrimmed. It happens to be byte-identical to its own rule's fullDescription.text and help.text, which is opengrep duplicating a finding's message into its rule descriptor -- captured output, not this adapter reaching for a rule string. no_synthesised_message.scoping_the_check_correctly states why that coincidence must not widen the prohibition check.
row_derivations.severity_native_note: the result states no level, and its rule carries neither properties.severity nor properties.problem.severity, so all three field sources AAP 0.5.4 authorises for a SARIF record are silent; the absence is stated rather than filled from rule.defaultConfiguration.level, which AAP 0.5.4 does not carry as a field source

cwe_source.text: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

row_derivations.anchor_note: This is the record the fixture retains to prove the adapter rejects one record while still emitting the other. Line 72 of the pinned DiskStore.scala is the interpolated string argument of the SparkException.internalError(...) call that opens on line 71, and the file is 380 lines, so start_line is within the file.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and the run_index / result_index pair name the same record. The pair is carried as well because normalize.adapters.sarif passes exactly run_index, result_index and rule_id into the rejection it builds at this step, so a produced Rejection's record_identity and this expectation can be compared directly, without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_MISSING_MESSAGE constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten, described there as "the record carries no message". Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.classification_step: step 3 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 and 2 pass on this record: it is a JSON object, and it carries a valid ruleId that resolves to /runs/0/tool/driver/rules/0 inside tool.driver.

defect_is_the_message_alone.statement: Asserted from the fixture, not assumed. Every other property of this record is well-formed, so nothing but the message can account for the rejection.
defect_is_the_message_alone.shape: a JSON object carrying level, locations, message, properties and ruleId -- so step 1 passes and malformed_record is not in play
defect_is_the_message_alone.rule_id: opt.blitzy-harness.rules.opengrep-rules.java.lang.correctness.hardcoded-conditional, a non-empty string that resolves by id to /runs/0/tool/driver/rules/0, so step 2 passes, rule_id_from_rule_id is bumped and rule_metadata_unresolved is not
defect_is_the_message_alone.path: common/network-shuffle/src/main/java/org/apache/spark/network/shuffle/OneForOneBlockPusher.java with uriBaseId %SRCROOT% -- a real file in the pinned tree, root-relative, resolvable through the same metadata-backed fallback the emitted row uses, and matching the allowlist glob common/network-shuffle/src/main/**. Had its message been usable it would have produced a kept row with in_scope true, which is the strongest available statement that step 4 is not what rejected it
defect_is_the_message_alone.start_line: 131, an integer, and within the file's 171 lines at the pin; the region's endLine of 137 and its snippet match the pinned source line for line, lines 131 to 137 being the if/else over PUSH_ERROR_HANDLER.shouldRetryError -- so step 5 would have passed too
defect_is_the_message_alone.severity: the record carries its own level of "error", so even severity would have resolved from the record itself without consulting its rule
defect_is_the_message_alone.conclusion: The message is the only defect, and the rejection is therefore attributable to it alone.

rejections.message_variant: message.text present as an empty string
rejections.expected_detail: the result's message.text is empty or whitespace only
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, and it is quoted here because this class covers four routes: naming the class alone would not distinguish an empty text from an absent message object, an absent text key or a non-string text. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings rather than by full-string equality. message_variants lists all four routes with the detail each produces.
rejections.steps_never_reached: Steps 4 and 5 never run, so this record's path is never resolved and its startLine of 131 is never examined -- neither unresolvable_path nor non_integer_start_line is in play, and neither could be, because both would require the record to have survived step 3. Worth stating because the fixture deliberately gives the defective record a real path and a valid line, and a reader could otherwise expect an interaction between the conditions.
rejections.record_identity_note: Exactly the three keys the adapter passes at this step. No uri and no uriBaseId appear, because those are added by the path resolver at step 4 and this record never reaches it -- so a test comparing record identities must expect three keys here and five on a path rejection. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no message to put in the row, and message is one of emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS rather than one of the five fields AAP 0.8.2 permits to be absent. So the record has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or synthesising a message from its rule -- would each hide it. Counting it under a named class keeps it visible and keeps the arithmetic honest.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so its level of "error" reaches no entry in severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none -- which is why severity_from_level is 0 here even though a level is present in the artifact.
rejections.contributes_no_message_text: Nothing from this record's message reaches any output. The empty string is not written into a row, and no substitute is written in its place.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.why_absent: this document is valid SARIF 2.1.0 and routes cleanly; its defect is one record, not its shape

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.cover_with: the sibling negative fixtures in this tree -- reject-sarif-malformed-record.sarif, reject-sarif-missing-rule-id.sarif, reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.sarif, reject-sarif-non-integer-start-line.sarif and the five reject-sarif-uribaseid-* fixtures. Which condition each of those asserts is stated in its own expected file, not here.

behaviours_not_exercised_by_this_fixture.cover_with: the derived fixtures named per variant under message_variants, and reject-sarif-malformed-record.sarif for the boundary
